hero.oneLiner: India's fastest growing packaged food company (among those with revenue above ₹15,000 million), exclusively focused on premium value-added dairy products under the 'Milky Mist' brand with an integrated farm-to-retail model built around a single Perundurai (Tamil Nadu) facility.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's fastest growing packaged food company (among those with revenue above ₹15,000 million), exclusively focused on premium value-added dairy products under the 'Milky Mist' brand with an integrated farm-to-retail model built around a single Perundurai (Tamil Nadu) facility.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Milky Mist manufactures and sells value-added dairy products - paneer, cheese, curd, butter, ghee, yogurt, ice cream and UHT long-shelf-life products - plus frozen foods, ready-to-eat/ready-to-cook meals and chocolates, offered under the umbrella brand 'Milky Mist' and sub-brands 'SmartChef', 'Capella', 'Misty Lite', 'Briyas' and 'Asal'. It sources raw milk directly from 74,654 farmers across 25 districts (all within a 400 km radius of its Perundurai plant) and processes it at a single U.S. FDA-approved manufacturing facility. Products reach consumers through general trade, modern trade, HoReCa, e-commerce/quick commerce, B2B bulk sales and 144 exclusive Milky Mist parlours, across 22 states and 5 union territories, with exports to more than 15 countries.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Asal Food Products Private Limited — Subsidiary (100%): Acquired from the Promoters pursuant to a share purchase agreement dated March 29, 2025 for consideration of ₹71.25 million; brought frozen foods, RTE and RTC products into the portfolio. 'Asal' brand contributed ₹460.56 million (1.47%) of FY2026 revenue from operations.
- Magiva Technologies Private Limited — Group Company: Sole Group Company; provides IT services to the Company (a related party transaction). Registered office at Erode, Tamil Nadu. Not listed on any stock exchange.
- Briyas Foods Private Limited — Asset seller / acquired brand: Asset purchase agreement dated February 19, 2025 for transfer of identified assets relating to its tofu business; 'Briyas' brand contributed ₹233.60 million (0.74%) of FY2026 revenue from operations.
- Sathishkumar T (Promoter) - trademark assignment — Related-party transaction: Trademark assignment deed dated July 15, 2025 assigning trademarks and associated goodwill to the Company for consideration of ₹88.60 million; one trademark is hypothecated as security for lender financing.
- Promoters as lessors — Related-party leases: Certain land leased by the Promoters to the Company for solar plants and chilling centres; Promoters have also extended guarantees for certain Company borrowings.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Integrated farm-to-retail model. BACKWARD: raw milk — the primary raw material — is sourced predominantly direct from farmers with no formal supply arrangements. As of March 31, 2026 the Company procured from 74,654 farmers (of whom 33,126 were women) across 25 districts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra, all within a 400 kilometre radius of Perundurai (67,615 farmers in Fiscal 2025; 67,807 in Fiscal 2024). Total raw milk procurement was 396.15, 307.20 and 272.80 million litres in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which 294.48 million litres (74.34%), 261.59 million litres (85.15%) and 263.55 million litres (96.61%) came directly from dairy farmers and 101.67 million litres (25.66%), 45.61 million litres (14.85%) and 9.25 million litres (3.39%) from third party dairy operators — the direct-from-farmer share has fallen sharply over the three years. Procurement is geographically concentrated in Tamil Nadu at 374.40 million litres (94.51%), 300.08 million litres (97.68%) and 271.77 million litres (99.62%); 'Others' (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh) was 21.75 million litres (5.49%), 7.12 million litres (2.32%) and 1.03 million litres (0.38%). Farmers are paid directly every 7 to 10 days, with middlemen eliminated; support includes cattle feed, silage training, fodder seeds, veterinary support, vaccinations, artificial insemination and cattle-loan facilitation, with 8, 10 and 28 farmer training programmes in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. A three-tier quality structure runs from 3,907 AMCUs (3 parameters) to 29 chilling centres comprising Milk Chilling Centres and Bulk Milk Coolers (21 parameters, located within a 30 to 40 kilometre radius of collection villages) to the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility (31 parameters). Realisation per litre of milk procured was approximately ₹77.79 in Fiscal 2026, stated to be the highest among listed peers (Source: 1Lattice Report). FORWARD: the Company operates its own logistics — as of March 31, 2026, 63 milk vans/tankers (average capacity 23,150 litres; 44 in Fiscal 2025 and 34 in Fiscal 2024), 282 reefer trucks with in-built refrigeration (payload approximately 10,485 kilograms; 252 in Fiscal 2025, 201 in Fiscal 2024) and 34 ambient trucks (payload approximately 24,350 kilograms; 21 in Fiscal 2025, 34 in Fiscal 2024), of which 26 owned vehicles are electric; IoT-enabled real-time fleet tracking and route optimisation, with return-load optimisation carrying third-party goods such as apples, cocoa powder, sweet corn, rice and butter. Stated to be the only dairy-focused company among its listed peers with entirely in-house logistics and manufacturing (Source: 1Lattice Report). Downstream cold chain at retail: 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed as of March 31, 2026, with a plan to deploy 30,000 ice cream freezers, 24,000 visi coolers and 12,000 chocolate coolers across Fiscals 2026, 2027 and 2028 funded partly from the Net Proceeds. Advertisement and business promotion expenses were ₹796.12 million (2.54% of revenue from operations), ₹711.32 million (3.03%) and ₹205.60 million (1.13%) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. FURTHER FORWARD INTEGRATION PLANNED from the Net Proceeds: whey protein concentrate capacity of 10 tons per day and edible/pharma-grade lactose capacity of 44 tons per day (moving whey powder up the value chain from a bulk commodity), a dedicated 60 TPD yogurt plant with packing lines rated at 50,800 containers per hour, a fresh cheese line for feta and gouda, processed-cheese capacity addition with a continuous cooker, and a dedicated warehouse for cold and dry products within the Perundurai facility.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Availability and price of raw milk - the primary raw material, procured with no formal supply arrangements from farmers; 94.51% of FY2026 raw milk came from Tamil Nadu, and volumes/prices swing with season, weather, cattle health and government policy
- Shift in procurement mix - direct-from-farmer share of total raw milk fell from 96.61% in FY2024 to 85.15% in FY2025 to 74.34% in FY2026 even as total procurement rose to 396.15 million litres
- Product mix toward high-margin value-added categories (cheese, cream, yogurt, curd, ice cream) and away from liquid milk, which the Company states typically carries lower profitability
- New product introductions and strategic acquisitions - 538 new SKUs since April 2022 contributed 28.16% of FY2026 revenue; the Asal and Briyas acquisitions added RTE/RTC and tofu
- Competition and pricing pressure - on-invoice and off-invoice discounting; off-invoice discounts were 4.99% of net invoice value in FY2026 versus 4.58% in FY2025 and 5.34% in FY2024
- Brand investment intensity - advertisement and business promotion expenses of ₹796.12 million in FY2026 (2.54% of revenue) versus ₹711.32 million (3.03%) in FY2025 and ₹205.60 million (1.13%) in FY2024
- Distribution network reach and cooler deployment at the point of sale as a driver of shelf space and offtake
- Capital intensity of the expansion programme - total capital expenditure of ₹5,771.79 million in FY2026 (18.39% of revenue from operations), ₹4,742.82 million in FY2025 and ₹2,882.56 million in FY2024
- Leverage and debt servicing - total borrowings of ₹16,718.53 million and a debt-to-equity ratio of 3.61 times as of March 31, 2026; aggregate fund-based outstanding borrowings of ₹13,907.23 million on a consolidated basis as of May 31, 2026
- Working capital cycle - 48 working capital days in FY2026 versus 42 in FY2025 and 49 in FY2024
- Government incentives and export benefits, including EPCG-linked duty savings
- Seasonality - winter flush season surplus milk is converted into cheddar cheese, UHT products and high-heat powder, while a 20% to 30% summer supply drop shifts production toward ice cream, beverages, curd and buttermilk

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen the Southern India position while building presence in the rest of India through e-commerce, quick commerce and modern trade, onboarding new distributors and increased advertising
- Deepen point-of-sale presence by deploying visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers funded partly from the Net Proceeds
- Expand the network of Milky Mist exclusive parlours into Karnataka, Maharashtra and Telangana to increase direct consumer reach
- Leverage international demand by focusing on additional export regions including Malaysia and New Zealand
- Expand production capacity at the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility by installing and commissioning whey protein concentrate and lactose manufacturing, a dedicated yogurt plant with packing lines, fresh cheese manufacturing, and processed cheese capacity addition
- Augment procurement capabilities by strengthening farmer relationships (incentives, cattle feed, veterinary care, artificial insemination, loan facilitation) and establishing additional tech-enabled AMCUs
- Further strengthen brand visibility and brand equity through traditional, social and digital advertising, brand ambassadors, sponsorships, influencer marketing and performance marketing
- Grow inorganically through strategic acquisitions that create synergies (no specific target identified or binding agreement entered into as of the date of the RHP)
- Leverage technology for operational and cost efficiency - advanced production automation, energy meters, expanding the Arasanur solar plant by 10 MW, a sludge digestion plant for natural gas, and data analytics with periodic third-party consumer surveys

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: All proposed expansion is at the existing single site in Perundurai, Erode District, Tamil Nadu - there is no new plant. The Company proposes to install and commission (i) a whey protein concentrate and lactose manufacturing line (approx. 10 TPD whey protein concentrate and 44 TPD edible/pharma-grade lactose) to forward-integrate the whey powder by-product out of bulk-commodity economics; (ii) a fully automated yogurt plant of 60 TPD with continuous filling lines packing 50,800 containers per hour; (iii) a fresh cheese line for feta and gouda variants to diversify beyond industrial cheddar, mozzarella, cream and processed cheese; and (iv) processed-cheese capacity addition via a continuous cooking system with cheese slice packing and overwrapping lines and a chiplet/cube packing line with automatic portion-packing. Alongside, a cold and dry warehouse and additional reefer and ambient trucks are planned. Separately, the Company states it is in the process of increasing cheddar cheese installed capacity from 15.6 MT per day to 120 MT per day, having already raised paneer capacity from 72 to 192 MT per day in Fiscal 2026, ghee from 24 to 48 MT per day in Fiscal 2026, whey powder from 36 to 104 tons per day in Fiscal 2025, and set curd from 120 to 240 MT per day and pouch curd from 240 to 480 MT per day in Fiscal 2025. Procurement infrastructure expands in parallel through additional AMCUs and chilling centres, and retail-facing expansion continues through exclusive parlours and cooler deployment.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fastest growing packaged food company in India among companies with revenue scale above ₹15,000 million, growing revenue at a 31.26% CAGR from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026 (Source: 1Lattice Report)
- Category leadership: largest private packaged paneer brand in the organised market (approx. 19.0% market share by value, FY2026); largest private packaged cheese brand in South India (approx. 12%) and third nationally among private players (approx. 5%); approx. 7% of the organised South India curd market; top-two private packaged yogurt brand (approx. 13%) and approx. 35-40% of the organised Greek yogurt market in India
- Premium pricing power - paneer and curd typically priced 10% to 30% above the average market price of large Indian brands, delivering the highest realisation per litre of milk procured among listed peers at approx. ₹77.79 in Fiscal 2026
- Integrated farm-to-retail infrastructure with direct sourcing from 74,654 farmers (33,126 women) via 3,907 AMCUs and 29 chilling centres, eliminating middlemen and paying farmers directly every 7 to 10 days
- Advanced, fully automated single-site manufacturing (robotic paneer line, automatic cheese-making with end-of-line automation, automated UHT lines, whey spray-drying) at a U.S. FDA approved facility, plus a milk balancing system that converts flush-season surplus into long-shelf-life products
- Diversified portfolio of 22 product categories and 640 SKUs with growth driven by category expansion rather than substitution; 538 new SKUs since April 2022 contributed 28.16% of FY2026 revenue
- Multi-channel distribution across 22 states and 5 union territories - 4,001 distributors, more than 375,000 retail touchpoints, 57 C&F depots, 144 exclusive parlours - reinforced by 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed as of March 31, 2026
- Self-managed, IoT-enabled cold-chain logistics (63 milk tankers, 282 reefer trucks, 34 ambient trucks) delivering one of the lowest transportation costs as a percentage of revenue among listed peers through return-load optimisation

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Single-site manufacturing concentration - all production runs through one facility at Perundurai, Erode, Tamil Nadu — Any shutdown, breakdown, natural disaster, labour action, regulatory suspension or loss of the U.S. FDA/food-safety approvals at this single site would halt essentially all output, and the Company also flags under-utilisation risk (paneer capacity utilisation fell to 52.44% in FY2026 from 110.49% in FY2025 after capacity was raised from 72 to 192 MT per day).
- Raw milk supply dependence concentrated in Tamil Nadu with no formal supplier agreements — Raw milk is the primary input for every product; 94.51%, 97.68% and 99.62% of procurement in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 came from Tamil Nadu, sourced from individual farmers with whom there are no binding contracts. Price and availability swing with season, weather, cattle health and state policy, feeding directly into cost of goods sold.
- Geographic revenue concentration in South India — South India generated 69.23%, 71.00% and 73.68% of revenue from operations in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. Regional competitive, regulatory or climatic shocks would hit the majority of the revenue base, and the rest-of-India build-out is still early.
- Substantial indebtedness and capital intensity — Total borrowings of ₹16,718.53 million with a 3.61x debt-to-equity ratio as of March 31, 2026 (₹13,907.23 million fund-based outstanding as of May 31, 2026). Capital expenditure ran at 15.82% to 20.19% of revenue over FY2024-FY2026, one trademark is hypothecated to lenders, Promoter guarantees back certain facilities, and ₹4,968.61 million of the Net Proceeds is earmarked simply to deleverage.
- Product concentration in paneer, cheese and curd — These three categories contributed 59.05%, 62.63% and 66.16% of revenue from operations in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. Failure to anticipate shifts in consumer taste, or a quality incident in any one of them, would disproportionately hit revenue.
- Perishability, cold-chain integrity and food-safety exposure — Shelf life ranges from 20 days to 12 months and products need chilled, ambient or frozen handling through an owned fleet. Spoilage, improper storage or transport, or a food-borne illness or allergen incident would trigger write-downs, product recalls, regulatory penalties and brand damage - the Company already faces FSSA proceedings over paneer samples in Ghaziabad.
- Working capital intensity and inventory/demand forecasting — Working capital days were 48, 42 and 49 in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. The Company flags that failure to arrange adequate working capital, or inaccurate demand forecasting against short-shelf-life inventory, would adversely affect operations.
- Contingent liabilities, tax disputes and auditor qualifications — Contingent liabilities aggregated ₹2,290.09 million as of March 31, 2026, of which ₹1,948.71 million is EPCG duty saved that becomes payable if export obligations are not met, plus ₹254.68 million of disputed statutory liabilities. Three indirect tax proceedings involving ₹313.91 million are outstanding, and the statutory auditors have included emphasis of matters and CARO/Rule 11(g) qualifications and adverse remarks for FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024.
